entities.summary: Agathodaemon of Alexandria was a Greek or Hellenized Egyptian cartographer, presumably from Alexandria, Roman Egypt, during late Antiquity, likely in the 2nd century AD. He is known for his work on the Ptolemaic map of the world, which was a highly influential and accurate representation of the known world at the time. Agathodaemon's map was likely created during the reign of the Roman Emperor Marcus Aurelius, and it is believed to have been used as a reference by later cartographers for centuries. The map's accuracy and detail were so impressive that it was even used by the Byzantine Empire to chart the Mediterranean Sea. Agathodaemon's work also had significant cultural and intellectual implications, as it highlighted the importance of geography and cartography in understanding the world. His contributions to the field of cartography paved the way for later cartographers, such as Ptolemy, and his work remains an important part of the history of science. Agathodaemon's legacy can be seen in the many copies of his map that have survived to this day, and his work continues to be studied by scholars and historians alike.
